name: Salary account standing orders dated the day before the salary stay a genuine shortfall, covered by at most two sources (G421)

expected.notes: G421. The honest counterpart to the on-payday scenario: the same salary account, but the three standing orders are dated Thu 26 Nov, one day BEFORE the Fri 27 Nov salary. Whatever the cause of that date, an outflow that lands before the income that funds it is a real gap in this window and is never hidden. Today is Wed 25 Nov, payday in 2 days, window 25 and 26 Nov. Barclays after payments = 600 - 150 (council tax) - 1,600 (standing orders) = -1,150, low point -1,150, short. The inbound legs are not credited to HSBC, NatWest or Monzo because their source Barclays is not itself covered that day, so those three keep 150, 120 and 80 and are not walked. Left to spend: the standing orders are own-account moves inside the pool, so only the council tax leaves it: 950 - 150 = 800. Cover plan (G421, at most two sources): the amount needed is ceil5(1,150) + 10 = 1,160. Headroom is balance minus the 10 buffer: HSBC 140, NatWest 110, Monzo 70. No single source covers it, so the two largest are used and never a third: HSBC 140 and NatWest 110, 250 in all, leaving 900 short after cover. Spend from after the earmark: HSBC 150 - 140 = 10, NatWest 120 - 110 = 10, Monzo 80, Barclays 0 (short). At risk count 1 (Barclays). G436 (Kevin 2026-11-07, every account in isolation, money in vs money out), which supersedes the Left to spend and Spend from figures worked above where they differ: Each account on its own, an own-account standing order being money out on its source and money in on its destination on its date, whether or not the source can afford it. Barclays 600 - 150 - 1,600 = -1,150; HSBC 150 + 900 = 1,050; NatWest 120 + 500 = 620; Monzo 80 + 200 = 280. -1,150 + 1,050 + 620 + 280 = 800, which is also the total of the four balances less the council tax (950 - 150): the transfers net to zero. Barclays stays flagged short (after payments -1,150, the G360 verdict and the cover engine are unchanged) and the two suggested moves are as before; after them Barclays -1,150 + 250 = -900, HSBC 1,050 - 140 = 910, NatWest 620 - 110 = 510, Monzo 280, sum 800 again. G438 (Kevin 2026-11-07): no own-account exemption. Every figure above is unchanged. Only the card's representative bill changes: the first item to bounce on Barclays is now named even when it is an own-account standing order. Walk on 26 Nov: 600 - 150 (council tax) = 450, then the 900 HSBC standing order takes it to -450, the first bounce, so the card names the 900 HSBC standing order (it used to name the council tax, because own-account orders were skipped).
